summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. Hidden information: estimateOpponentRanges reads only PlayerView fields (seat, holeCards, board, players, actions, button via positionOf); dead cards are the viewer's hole cards plus the board only. earlierShowdowns, other seats' hole cards, the deck and HandState are never read (grep confirms), so earlier showdowns are not treated as dead. REQ-035.3: bots now pass adviceOptions(options), which copies only equity/chart/opponentRanges, and recommend/recommendPostflop/gradeView use an ExactOptions guard that makes extra keys such as style a type error; ranges.ts and postflop.ts import nothing from src/bots. JSON: six-max.json is bundled, authored data validated at import. parseDefaultRanges never indexes objects with untrusted keys (it uses a Map and a find over the fixed APPLICABLE_LINES list), so __proto__/constructor keys only produce 'does not apply' problems. Hand-class regexes are anchored with no nested quantifiers (no ReDoS), and malformed tokens or reversed ranks are rejected. Untrusted text in error messages is cut to 20 characters. Worker boundary: handleAdviceRequest still checks shape and turns every throw into ok:false; the only change is the options constant passed to recommend/gradeView. Bad views (board shorter than 3 or longer than 5) throw RangeError, which is caught there. Work per request is bounded (at most 1326 combos x 3 streets x 5 opponents). No new dependencies, randomness, secrets or I/O. The range content and justifications are original prose with no third-party attribution or copied chart text, consistent with REQ-061.
